speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when this weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm started, and did it begin suddenly or gradually?

text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain radiating from your neck into your arm, or is the weakness isolated to the limb? I also need to know if you have experienced any difficulty with your vision, speech, or balance.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the significant weight loss, history of alcohol and steroid use, and focal neurological deficits, I am concerned for a malignant process like Pancoast tumor or lymphoma rather than simple neuropathy. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
